note: Shared hardening fixtures. The single source of truth for when a commitment's
correction window closes, consumed by BOTH implementations of the rule:
public.earned_hardens_at (SQL). Neither may drift from the other, because the
server decides independently whether an override request is against a hardened
contract and must reach the same answer the device does.
hardensAt = createdAt + min(correctionWindow, max(0, deadline - createdAt) * 0.125)
Times are UTC ISO-8601. correctionWindow is seconds. Expected values were
computed by a third implementation, so a shared bug in Swift and SQL still fails.
The DST cases exist to catch calendar-day interval arithmetic in Postgres:
three days must mean 72 hours of absolute time, whatever the session timezone.

cases.name: clamp binds: a two-hour fuse hardens after fifteen minutes
clamp binds: fourteen hours out, still short of the configured window
exact tie: sixteen hours out makes clamp and configured window equal
configured window binds: a plan occurrence four weeks out
deadline equal to creation leaves no window
deadline before creation is clamped at zero, never negative
fractional creation instant is carried through exactly
clamp lands on a fractional second
an eight-second fuse hardens after one second
DST fall-back: three days is 72 hours, not three calendar days
DST spring-forward: three days is 72 hours, not three calendar days
